Subject: Realtime: p95 spike + 502s across private deployment in us-west

Aditya / Marissa,

We're seeing a sustained p95 latency increase to ~2.3s (baseline ~450ms) starting at 07:45 PDT. Concurrently, about 4-6% of requests to our private VPC endpoint are returning 502/504. This is affecting LLM-assisted triage in production — backlog is growing and users are timeouting.

Quick facts:
- Topology: private deployment (multi-node, GPU pool) in us-west-2, customer-managed VPC
- Traffic: steady at ~1.8k rps for inference; peak bursts to 2.3k rps observed during the window
- Error pattern: 502/504s, some 500s; no obvious upstream (internal service) errors in our app logs

Attached is a short telemetry snapshot and a tail of 502 responses (lucentcare_telemetry_snapshot_0830.zip). Can Redwood ops/engineering triage? This is impacting clinical workflows.

We need immediate steps we can take to mitigate and an ETA for a permanent fix. Please escalate if this needs broader attention.

— Helen
LucentCare Ops

Subject: Re: Realtime: p95 spike + 502s across private deployment in us-west

Initial triage notes (10:30):
- Observed pattern: bursty token-generation loops correlated with one model serving process exhausting GPU memory and forcing frequent small restarts (~1 every 3–5m on node-3). That causes transient 502s and elevated end-to-end latency.
- KV cache: drop in prefix-cache hit ratio on node-3 from 92% -> 56% in the window. Suggests cache thrash on the hot node.
- Queues: per-node request queue length on node-3 is spiking; other nodes ~stable.

Immediate mitigations executed (10:20–10:28):
- Disabled opportunistic dynamic batching on node-3 (to avoid oversized batches triggering OOM).
- Applied conservative CPU affinity adjustment for the runtime process and increased the KV cache size on node-3 by +18%.
- Brought up an additional warm standby on the same pool and rebalanced routing for 30% of incoming traffic to it.

Early result: error rate dropped from 5.1% -> 1.4% and p95 reduced to ~1.1s (from 2.3s). Still above baseline.

Next steps (ETA 2 hours for full stabilization):
- Provision an extra node in the private pool (customer approval required if out-of-commit).
- Run quick model-quantization profile on the hot shard to test lower memory footprint and validate no quality regression (can be done on standby node).
- Follow-up: Jonas to produce a short postmortem of root cause and an ops playbook to avoid recurrence.

Logs: attached small debug sample (LUC-2389-debug-sample.log).

— Irene
SRE Lead, Runtime Reliability | Redwood Inference
